abstract: Children fathered by 27 testicular cancer patients treated with radiotherapy, 25 treated with chemotherapy, and 57 control men (46 community controls and 11 Stage I testicular cancer patients) were examined for evidence of congenital malformations. The proportion of malformations in children in the treatment group did not differ from that in children in the control group or from incidence rates for malformations in the general population. Our results suggest that treatment for testicular cancer should not constitute a reason for advising termination of pregnancy, although numbers were too few to detect a relative risk smaller than 3 X 2. More observations are needed to provide a definite answer.
abstract_ja: 放射線療法を受けた精巣がん患者27例、化学療法を受けた25例、対照男性57例（地域住民対照46例、病期Iの精巣がん患者11例）の子どもについて、先天奇形の有無を検討した。治療群の子どもにおける奇形の割合は、対照群や一般集団の発生率と差がなかった。本研究の結果は、精巣がんの治療を理由に妊娠中絶を勧めるべきではないことを示唆する。ただし、症例数は相対危険度3×2未満の差を検出するには不十分であった。さらなる観察が必要である。
